data.name: Rumi
data.gender_notes: Rumi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rumi is a term used to describe a poem or ode written in praise of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The name Rumi carries the meaning “Ode to the Prophet” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Rumi usually hope their child will grow to embody ode to the prophet and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To recite the praise and glorify the Prophet
data.etymology: Rumi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ode to the Prophet.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rumi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: رومي
in_arabic.meaning: المقصود بالروح أو المكان المقدس الروحاني
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مشتق من كلمة 'روح' التي تعني الروح أو النفس، ويرتبط بالبعد الروحاني والمقدس. يشير إلى مدينة روما أو الأشخاص المرتبطين بها، ولكنه في السياق الإسلامي يحمل معاني أعمق تتعلق بالروحانية والإيمان.

in_urdu.name: رومی
in_urdu.meaning: روحانی یا مقدس مقام سے متعلق
in_urdu.long_meaning: رومی ایک نام ہے جو لفظ 'روح' سے ماخوذ ہے، جو روح یا نفس کے معنی میں ہے۔ یہ نام روحانی اور مقدس مفاهیم کے ساتھ منسلک ہے، خاص طور پر رومی سلطنت یا روم سے متعلق جغرافیائی علاقے کے ساتھ۔ اسلامی ثقافت میں، یہ نام روحانی اہمیت اور علم اور حکمت کی تلاش کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: रोमी
in_hindi.meaning: आध्यात्मिक या पवित्र स्थान से संबंधित
in_hindi.long_meaning: रोमी नाम 'روح' शब्द से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है आत्मा या आत्मा। यह नाम आध्यात्मिक और पवित्र अवधारणाओं से जुड़ा है, विशेष रूप से रोमन साम्राज्य या रोम से जुड़े भौगोलिक क्षेत्र से। इस्लामी संस्कृति में, यह नाम आध्यात्मिक महत्व और ज्ञान और ज्ञान की खोज को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: رومي
in_pashto.meaning: روحاني یا سپېڅلی ځای سره تړاو
in_pashto.long_meaning: رومي د (روح) کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی نوم دی، چې د روح یا نفس معنی لري. دا نوم روحاني او سپېڅلو مفهومونو سره تړاو لري، په ځانګړي ډول د رومي امپراتورۍ یا د روم سره تړلي جغرافيايي ساحې سره. په اسلامي کلتور کې، دا نوم روحاني اهميت او د پوهې او حکمت د لټون څرګندوي.

in_english.name: Rumi
in_english.long_meaning: Rumi is a name derived from the Arabic root 'Rūḥ', meaning spirit, soul, or essence. It is linked to spirituality, mysticism, and the city of Rome. In Islamic tradition, the name Rumi holds significance due to its association with Jalāl ad-Dīn Muhammad Rūmī, a renowned Sufi poet and philosopher. The name embodies qualities of spiritual depth, wisdom, and enlightenment.

data.cultural_impact: Rumi, also known as Jalal al-Din Muhammad Balkhi or Mawlana Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi, (1207-1273 CE) was a 13th-century Persian poet, philosopher, and Sufi theologian. His poetry transcended cultural and linguistic barriers, influencing the works of poets, such as Hafez and Shakespeare. A legend once said that upon hearing Rumi’s poetry, St. Thomas a Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury in England, wept upon hearing a translation of his works from Latin.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rumi derives from the Arabic word 'rumi', which means 'a Roman' or a 'dweller in Rome'. However, the term came to be used as a term for Sufis, and has been associated with Mawlana Jalal al-Din Rumi, the famous Persian poet, and for his spiritual teachings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Ode to the Prophet" symbolizes Rumi is a term used to describe a poem or ode written in praise of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Rumi serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of ode to the prophet.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi was a 13th century Persian poet, jurist, theologian, and Sufi mystic. The name Rumi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Rumi was a prominent figure in the Persian world, and his poetry and teachings continue to influence Sufi thought and practice.

trends: Rumi's poetry is popular in the modern world, with translations and adaptations being widely read.
Rumi's teachings on love and spirituality continue to inspire people around the world.
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Rumi remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
